My published and in-progress work concerns how deep-learning models for RNA secondary structure are evaluated, and how they can be made to generalize beyond the families they were trained on. An up-to-date list is also available on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=mBucAygAAAAJ&hl=en).

## Articles and Preprints

::: {.publication}
Bugnon, L. A., **Kulemeyer, G.**, Gerard, M., Di Persia, L., Stegmayer, G., & Milone, D. H. (2026). *Homology-aware cross-validation strategies for generalization assessment in RNA structure prediction.*

::: {.publication-meta}
Under review · bioRxiv preprint
:::

The paper examines how homology between training and test sequences inflates reported accuracy in RNA structure prediction, and compares classical and deep-learning predictors under family-aware and sequence-similarity validation schemes. My contribution centers on the comparative benchmarking and its reproducible implementation.

::: {.publication-links}
[Preprint (DOI)](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.06.28.735057) · [Code and data](https://github.com/sinc-lab/xvalRNAfolding)
:::
:::

## In Preparation

::: {.publication}
*The Less the Better: Improving RNA Secondary Structure Generalization with Structural-Aware Subsampling.*

::: {.publication-meta}
Manuscript in preparation
:::

Structure-aware subsampling of training data retains roughly 18% of ArchiveII while preserving structural diversity, reaching performance comparable to training on the full dataset. The manuscript reports the subsampling strategy and its effect on cross-family generalization.
:::
